OpenFoldPanel / ARCHIVE

Structure

Secondary Structure

Helix Alpha-helical secondary structure segment.
Strand Beta-strand segment with chain direction indicated.
Turn Turn region connecting distinct secondary structure elements.

Tracks

Sequence and Physicochemical Tracks

A Query Sequence Residue letter cell for the target sequence at this position.
A Exact Match Residue is identical to the query sequence at this position.
S Similar Substitution Residue differs from the query but remains a conservative substitution.
Accessibility / Buried Dark blue indicates very low surface accessibility and mostly buried residues.
Accessibility / Intermediate Grey-blue indicates partial exposure between buried and exposed states.
Accessibility / Accessible Light blue indicates residues that are more solvent-accessible.
Accessibility / Highly Exposed Gold indicates residues with strong surface exposure.
Hydropathy / Hydrophobic Orange indicates locally hydrophobic regions, often buried or lipid-facing.
Hydropathy / Neutral Gray indicates locally intermediate physicochemical character.
Hydropathy / Hydrophilic Blue indicates locally hydrophilic regions with stronger aqueous compatibility.

Confidence Tracks

Very High pLDDT ≥ 90 indicates very high local confidence.
Confident 70 ≤ pLDDT < 90 indicates a generally reliable region.
Low 50 ≤ pLDDT < 70 indicates limited confidence and should be interpreted carefully.
Very Low pLDDT < 50 indicates an unstable or weakly predicted region.

Contacts

Contact Strength and Symbols

Strong Protein Contact Based on the shortest non-hydrogen atom distance: below 3.2 A.
Weak Protein Contact Based on the shortest non-hydrogen atom distance: between 3.2 A and 3.7 A, inclusive.
Intramolecular Disulfide Green S marks a CYS-CYS disulfide bond within the same protein chain.
Intermolecular Disulfide Cyan S marks a CYS-CYS disulfide bond between different protein chains.
Same-position Protein Contact Contact partners share the same residue number and residue identity.
Ion Indicates a contact with an ion partner.
Nucleic Acid Indicates a contact with a nucleic-acid partner.
Porphyrin-like Ligand Indicates contact with a porphyrin or related macrocyclic ligand.
Glycan Indicates contact with a carbohydrate ligand.
Other Ligand Indicates contact with another non-protein, non-nucleic-acid, non-glycan partner.
Multiple Contacts Indicates multiple contact types at the same residue position.
